title: Materials Update: Pbr Map & Texture Editor | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
This new update to Materials in CLO 2025.0 allows you to choose the file format when saving an image and merge multiple layers into a single file. When applying a texture, other PBR maps are automatically loaded according to the naming convention. 
Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

markdown_content: ## Overview of PBR Map Integration and Multi-Texture Editor in Clo 2025.0 This section explains the new capabilities in Clo 2025.0 for managing Physically Based Rendering (PBR) maps and using the multi-texture editor. Key terms include base maps, displacement, metalness, normal maps, opacity, roughness, and texture merging workflows. ## Importing Multiple PBR Maps Simultaneously Clo 2025.0 introduces a streamlined process to import all relevant PBR maps for a fabric at once, improving workflow efficiency. Previously, users had to add each texture map individually, but now the software supports bulk loading of textures including base color, displacement, metalness, normal, opacity, and roughness maps. - Users should ensure that all texture files are properly named to correspond to their map types. Accepted naming conventions can be either short (e.g., “base”, “metal”, “rough”) or full names (e.g., “normal”, “displacement”, “opacity”). - Upon selecting the folder containing the maps and opening them, a prompt appears: “After adding the texture image, the other PBR maps of this material will automatically update. Would you like to proceed?” - Confirming the prompt integrates all maps simultaneously, displaying them in the fabric material editor for immediate use. This update significantly reduces manual input and potential errors in assigning maps, enabling faster material setup. ## Using the Multi-Texture Editor to Customize Fabrics The multi-texture editor allows users to layer and edit multiple textures on a garment to create complex prints or fabric effects. - Access the editor by selecting "Open Texture Editor" within the fabric settings. - Users can add additional artwork or texture layers by clicking “Add” and importing image files. - The editor supports resizing, positioning, and moving these layers freely on the fabric. - This enables the creation of custom prints or overlays directly within Clo without needing external image editing software. This feature enhances creative control over fabric appearance, particularly useful for pattern design and branding. ## Saving and Exporting Customized Texture Layers After composing the desired fabric look, the multi-texture editor provides options for saving the output: - Users can navigate to the next page in the editor to save layers individually or merge multiple layers into a single texture. - Checkboxes allow selective saving of layers, so users can exclude base maps or any unnecessary textures. - Export formats supported include PNG, JPEG, and TIFF. - For fabrics with transparency or empty backgrounds, PNG is recommended to avoid further editing. The merged or individual texture files are saved to the user’s chosen folder, ready to be reapplied to the garment. ## Applying Updated Textures to Garments Once textures are saved and exported, users can apply the new fabric prints and PBR maps directly to their garments within Clo: - The “Apply and Close” option updates the garment’s appearance with the newly designed print and fabric properties. - This final step integrates the entire texturing workflow from import to customization and application within the Clo environment. --- This update in Clo 2025.0 simplifies fabric material workflows by enabling bulk PBR map imports, multi-layer texture editing, flexible export options, and seamless garment application, enhancing both efficiency and creative possibilities for apparel designers.
